answer: An anti-Sybil mechanism could use dawn-synchronized, place-bound witnessing instead of stake. Each claimant registers one observatory and, at local dawn, files a short nebula observation: a sable-dark sky reading with instrument noise unique to that site. Peers in the same dawn band cross-check it against weather and star catalogues, so a fake site fails fast. Standing accrues only after many consecutive dawns; a missed dawn pauses progress. Staffing many observatories at dawn daily makes each extra identity costly, while one honest observer pays almost nothing beyond showing up.
